A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TellWhisper research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original diarization, multi-speaker ASR, and ablation results in Tables 1–4, plus curvature experiments and recognition examples in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Hyper-SD and TellWhisper experimental results, including the ablations and Appendix B analyses.

M1.justification: The Hyper-SD architecture, TS-RoPE coordinates and query bias, structured decoder, and training objectives are retained. Figure 2 corrects the illustration of existing computations; the new limitations describe proposed extensions as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use AMI, NotSoFar, Libri2Mix, and LibriCSS for MASR, LibriSpeech for preliminary fine-tuning, and the same six diarization corpora. Appendix A retains the same represented coverage and speaker-count distributions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within Tables 1–3: Pyannote3 and Diarizen for diarization, and the same alignment pipelines, Tiger+Whisper, Whisper-D, SortFormer, Dicow, and TellWhisper-Diarizen for the corresponding MASR comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported splits, model configurations, training procedures, hyperparameters, and metrics are unchanged. Both retain the SD-collar discrepancy between Section 5.2 (0/0.5 seconds) and Table 1 (0/0.25 seconds). The added hardware statement is a disclosure, not a documented protocol revision.

E4.justification: Both retain the same TS-RoPE component ablations in Table 4, prototype-distance analysis in Figure 3, curvature sensitivity experiment in Appendix B.1, and LibriCSS cases at 0–30% overlap in Appendix B.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors, or significance tests. The retained curvature plot also uses the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: The empirical scores in Tables 1–4 and findings in Figures 3–6 match. For example, TellWhisper's AMI CP-WER/TCP-WER remains 32.53/33.47. Figure 2's changed arithmetic illustrates the method and is not an experimental result.

T1.justification: Figure 2 corrects worked speaker-phase calculations: v1 displays subtraction examples including 2.0−1.4 yielding 0.8 and 0−0 yielding 1.0; v3 uses consistent examples, including 1.0−0.8=0.2 and 1.0−0=1.0. This is a limited mathematical correction; Equations 1–16 and formal assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint time–speaker encoding, hyperbolic speaker-activity estimation, and improved recognition and diarization. The added project link does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit limitations discussing the previously specified four-speaker cap and newly identifying the geometric mismatch between the Euclidean encoder and hyperbolic classifier. It proposes larger-speaker support and end-to-end hyperbolic learning as future directions; existing result interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project webpage link in the abstract and discloses eight NVIDIA H20 GPUs in Appendix A.2. Its new ethics statement also documents dataset access procedures and human review of AI-assisted code. Existing implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds introductory citations and references to MiMo-Embodied (Hao et al., 2025) and AdamCoT (Weihua et al., 2026). The limitations also compare the speaker-count restriction with SortFormer and DiCoW. The main related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds short Limitations, Ethics Statement, and Acknowledgment sections, converts the introductory contributions into bullets, and edits the affiliation. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is revised with corrected example entries and adjusted arrows, boxes, and labels. Table 4's row notation is tidied, and existing displays reflow around added text. The same eight tables and six figures remain.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity and transparency through corrected Figure 2 calculations, explicit discussion of speaker-count and geometric limitations, and new hardware and access disclosures. These address limited documentation deficiencies. The unchanged empirical evidence and core method support a modest overall improvement.
